why: The message in the queue expired. The sending server tried to relay or deliver the message, but the action wasn't completed before the message expiration time. This message can also indicate that a message header limit was reached on a remote server, or some other protocol timeout occurred during server communication.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the receiving server. Check the validity of the recipient address, and determine whether the receiving server is configured correctly to receive messages.  You might have to reduce the number of recipients in the message header for the host about which you're receiving this error. If you send the message again, the message is placed in the queue again. If the receiving server is available, the message is delivered.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 4.4.7 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-4-4-7-in-exchange-online).

why: The destination MX host isn't the expected host per the domain's Strict Transport Security (STS) policy.
fix: This error usually indicates that the destination domain's MTA-STS policy doesn't contain the MX host. For more information, see [Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS](/en-us/purview/enhancing-mail-flow-with-mta-sts).

why: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 is trying to send a message to an email server outside Microsoft 365 or Office 365, but all attempts to connect are failing because of a network connection issue at the external server's location.
fix: This error almost always indicates an issue that affects the receiving server or network outside of Microsoft 365 or Office 365. The error should also include the IP address of the server or service that's generating the error. You can use this address to identify the party that's responsible for fixing this issue.

why: The message has more than 200 SMTP envelope recipients from the same domain.
fix: An envelope recipient is the original, unexpanded recipient that's used in the **RCPT TO** command to transmit the message between SMTP servers. If Microsoft 365 or Office 365 returns this error, the sending server must break up the number of envelope recipients into smaller chunks (chunking) and resend the message.

why: The destination mail server's certificate must chain to a trusted root Certificate Authority and the Common Name or Subject Alternative Name must contain an entry for the host name in the STS policy.
fix: This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server's certificate. For more information, see [Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS](/en-us/purview/enhancing-mail-flow-with-mta-sts).

sample: `Access denied, a message sent over IPv6 [2a01:111:f200:2004::240] must pass either SPF or DKIM validation, this message is not signed`
why: The sending message sent over IPv6 must pass either SPF or DKIM.
fix: For more information, see [Support for anonymous inbound email messages over IPv6](/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/support-for-anonymous-inbound-email-messages-over-ipv6).

sample: `starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail.`
why:
- DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server doesn't respond to the `STARTTLS` command.
- The destination server responds to the `STARTTLS` command, but the TLS handshake fails.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address. Determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive the messages.

sample: `certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate is expired.`
why: DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server provides an expired certificate.
fix: A valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired must be presented. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, most commonly on an annual basis.

why:
Records are DNSSEC authentic, but one or multiple of these scenarios occurred:
- The destination mail server's certificate doesn't match the authentic TLSA record requirements.
- Authentic TLSA record is misconfigured.
- Destination domain is being attacked.
- Any other DANE failure.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see [DANE protocol: updates and operational guidance](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7671).

sample: `dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records`
why: The destination domain indicated that it was DNSSEC-authentic, but Exchange Online wasn't able to verify it as DNSSEC-authentic.
fix: For more information, see [Overview of DNSSEC.](/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/jj200221%28v=ws.11%29)

sample: `certificate-host-mismatch: Remote certificate MUST have a common name or subject alternative name that matches the hostname (DANE)`
why: This error occurs if the presented certificate identities (CN and SAN) of a destination SMTP target host don't match any of the domains or MX host.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see [How SMTP DNS-based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) works to secure email communications](/en-us/microsoft-365/compliance/how-smtp-dane-works).

why: Suspicious activity was detected and sending was temporarily restricted for further evaluation.
fix: If this activity is valid, this restriction is lifted shortly.

why: Suspicious activity was detected on the IP in question, and the address is temporarily restricted while being further evaluated.
fix: If this activity is valid, this restriction is lifted shortly.

sample: Generic error, `x-dg-ref header is too long`, or `Requested action not taken: policy violation detected (AS345)`
why: 5.0.350 is a generic catch-all error code for a wide variety of nonspecific errors from the recipient's email organization. The specific `x-dg-ref header is too long` message is related to Rich Text-formatted messages. The specific `Requested action not taken: policy violation detected (AS345)` message is related to nested attachments.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.0.350 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-0-350-in-exchange-online).

why: This NDR commonly occurs when someone saves an email message to a file in Outlook, opens it offline, and then replies. The message property preserves only the **legacyExchangeDN** attribute when Outlook delivers the message. Therefore, the lookup could fail.
fix: Either the recipient address is incorrectly formatted or the recipient couldn't be correctly resolved. The first step to resolve this error is to check the recipient address, and send the message again.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.0 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-1-0-in-exchange-online).

why:
The following conditions might cause this failure:
- The sender incorrectly entered the recipient's email address.
- The recipient's email address doesn't exist in the destination email system.
- The recipient's mailbox was moved, and the sender’s Outlook recipient cache didn't update.
- An invalid legacy domain name (DN) exists for the recipient's mailbox Active Directory Domain Service.
fix: This error typically occurs if the sender of the message enters an incorrect email address of the recipient. The sender should check the recipient's email address and send again. This error can occur if the recipient’s email address was previously valid but later changed or removed.  If the sender of the message is in the same organization as the recipient, and the recipient's mailbox still exists, determine whether the recipient's mailbox was relocated to a new email server. If so, Outlook might not update the recipient cache correctly. Instruct the sender to remove the recipient's address from sender's Outlook recipient cache, and then create a new message. Resending the original message causes the same failure.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.1 through 5.1.20 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-1-1-through-5-1-20-in-exchange-online).

why: The account was blocked for sending too much spam. Typically, this problem occurs because the account was compromised (hacked) by phishing or malware.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.1.8 in Exchange Online](https://support.microsoft.com/topic/e323f21d-4460-4be1-999c-c9c0cc6be4b4).

why: SMTP address lookup didn't find the recipient's `<SMTP Address>`.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.1.10 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-1-10-in-exchange-online).

sample: `Your message can't be sent because you've reached your daily limit for message recipients`
why: The sender exceeded the recipient rate limit, as described in [Sending limits](/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-service-description/exchange-online-limits#sending-limits).
fix: This error could indicate that the account was compromised and is being used to send spam. For more information, see [Responding to a compromised account](/en-us/defender-office-365/responding-to-a-compromised-email-account).

why: The sender exceeded the recipient rate limit or the message rate limit as described in [Sending limits](/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/exchange-online-service-description/exchange-online-limits#sending-limits).
fix: This error could indicate the account was compromised and is being used to send spam. For more information, see [Responding to a compromised account](/en-us/defender-office-365/responding-to-a-compromised-email-account).

sample: `Recipient's per hour message receive limit from specific sender exceeded`
why: The sender exceeded the maximum number of messages that they're allowed to send per hour to a specific recipient in Exchange Online.
fix: The automated mailer or sender should try again later, and reduce the number of messages that they send per hour to a specific recipient.  This limit helps protect Microsoft 365 and Office 365 users from rapidly filling their Inboxes with many messages from errant automated notification systems or other single-sender mail storms.  The ["Mailboxes exceeding receiving limits"](/en-us/exchange/monitoring/mail-flow-reports/mailboxes-exceeding-receiving-limits-report) report shows detailed information about the mailboxes that are receiving large volumes of messages in a short time.

sample: `Recipient's per hour message receive limit exceeded`
why: The Microsoft 365 or Office 365 recipient exceeded the number of messages that they can receive per hour from all senders.
fix: The automated mailer or sender should try again later, and reduce the number of messages that they send per hour to a specific recipient.  This limit helps protect Microsoft 365 and Office 365 users from rapidly filling their Inboxes with many messages from errant automated notification systems or other mail storms.  The ["Mailboxes exceeding receiving limits"](/en-us/exchange/monitoring/mail-flow-reports/mailboxes-exceeding-receiving-limits-report) report shows detailed information about the mailboxes that are receiving large volumes of messages in a short time.

sample: `Journaling on-premises messages to Microsoft 365 or Office 365 not supported when Journaling Archive is disabled`
why: Journaling on‑premises messages to Microsoft 365 or Office 365 isn’t supported for this organization because Journaling Archive isn’t enabled in the organization’s settings.
fix: A journaling rule is configured in the organization's on-premises environment to journal on-premises messages to Microsoft 365 or Office 365, but Journaling Archive is disabled. For this scenario to work, the organization's Office 365 administrator should either enable Journaling Archive or change the journaling rule to journal messages to a different location.

why: The mail server that's generating the error doesn't accept mail for the recipient's domain. Mail server or DNS misconfiguration causes this error.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.4.1 in Exchange Online](https://support.microsoft.com/topic/c0e98a8e-81db-49c2-9bf1-32a1734d3e77).

why: The recipient's address doesn't exist.
fix: For more information, see [Use Directory Based Edge Blocking to reject messages sent to invalid recipients](/en-us/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/use-directory-based-edge-blocking).

why: A configuration error caused an email loop. On-premises Exchange server generates error 5.4.6 (you see this code in hybrid environments). Exchange Online generates error 5.4.14.  By default, after 20 iterations of an email loop, Exchange interrupts the loop and generates an NDR to the sender of the message.
fix: This error occurs if the delivery of a message generates another message in response. That message then generates a third message, and the process is repeated, creating a loop. To help protect against exhausting system resources, Exchange interrupts the mail loop after 20 iterations. Mail loops are typically created because of a configuration error on the sending mail server, the receiving mail server, or both. To determine whether automatic message forwarding is enabled, check the sender's and recipient's mailbox rules configuration.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.4.6 or 5.4.14 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-4-6-through-5-4-20-in-exchange-online).

why: The destination MX host wasn't the host expected per the domain's STS policy.
fix: This error usually indicates that the destination domain's MTA-STS policy doesn't contain the MX host. For more information, see [Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS](/en-us/purview/enhancing-mail-flow-with-mta-sts).

why: The email message wasn't delivered in time. The destination server didn't respond, or an error occurred, and the NDR could not be delivered to the sender.

sample: `550 5.5.0 Requested action not taken: mailbox unavailable`
why: The recipient's `<SMTP Address>` domain is @hotmail.com or @outlook.com and it wasn't found by SMTP address lookup.
fix: Similar to 550 5.1.10. For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.1.10 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-1-10-in-exchange-online).

why: Your email program added invalid characters (bare line feed characters) to a message that you sent.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.6.11 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-6-11-in-exchange-online).

why: The sender of the message isn't allowed to send messages to the recipient.
fix: This error occurs if the sender tries to send a message to a recipient but the sender isn't authorized to send one. This error frequently occurs when a sender tries to send messages to a distribution group that's configured to accept messages only from members of that distribution group or other authorized senders. The sender must request permission to send messages to the recipient.  This error can also occur if an Exchange transport rule rejects a message because the message matched conditions that are configured on the transport rule.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-7-1-in-exchange-online).

why: The sending email system isn't allowed to send a message to an email system that isn't the final destination of the message.
fix:
This error occurs if the sending email system tries to send an anonymous message to a receiving email system, and the receiving email system doesn't accept messages for the domain or domains that are specified in one or more of the recipients. The following are the most common cause of this error:
- A third party tries to use a receiving email system to send spam, and the receiving email system rejects the attempt. By the nature of spam, the sender's email address might be forged, and the resulting NDR could have been sent to the unsuspecting sender's email address. It's difficult to avoid this situation.
- An MX record for a domain points to a receiving email system where that domain isn't accepted. The administrator responsible for the specific domain name must correct the MX record or configure the receiving email system to accept messages sent to that domain, or do both.
- A sending email system or client that should use the receiving email system to relay messages doesn't have the correct permissions to do this.

For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-7-1-in-exchange-online).

why: The sending email system didn't authenticate with the receiving email system. The receiving email system requires authentication before message submission.
fix: This error occurs if the receiving server must be authenticated before message submission, and the sending email system isn't authenticated with the receiving email system. The sending email system administrator must configure the sending email system to authenticate with the receiving email system for delivery to be successful.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.1 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-550-5-7-1-in-exchange-online).

why: The destination mail server's certificate must chain to a trusted root Certificate Authority and the Common Name or Subject Alternative Name must contain an entry for the host name in the STS policy.
fix: This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server's certificate. For more information, see [Enhancing mail flow with MTA-STS](/en-us/purview/enhancing-mail-flow-with-mta-sts).

why: The sender's message is rejected because the recipient address is set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.12 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-12-in-exchange-online).

sample: `The message was rejected because of Sender Policy Framework violation`
why: The destination email system uses SPF to validate inbound mail, and an issue affects your SPF configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.23 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-23-in-exchange-online).

sample: `Access denied, the sending IPv6 address [2a01:111:f200:2004::240] must have a reverse DNS record`
why: The sending IPv6 address must have a reverse DNS record to send email over IPv6.
fix: For more information, see [Support for anonymous inbound email messages over IPv6](/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/support-for-anonymous-inbound-email-messages-over-ipv6).

sample: `Client was not authenticated to send anonymous mail during MAIL FROM`
why: You configured an application or device to send (relay) email messages in Microsoft 365 or Office 365 using the smtp.office365.com endpoint, and an issue affects the configuration of the application or device.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.57 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-57-in-exchange-online).

why: You use an inbound connector to receive messages from your on-premises email environment, and something changed in your on-premises environment that makes the inbound connector's configuration incorrect.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.64 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-64-in-exchange-online).

why: The sender doesn't have permission to send to the distribution group because the sender isn't in the group's allowed-senders list. Depending how the group is set up, even the group's owner might have to be added to the allowed sender list in order to send messages to the group.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.124 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-124-in-exchange-online).

why: The recipient address is a group distribution list that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization or the group owner can change this configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.133 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-133-in-exchange-online).

why: The recipient address is a mailbox that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.134 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-134-in-exchange-online).

sample: `Sender was not authenticated for public folder`
why: The recipient address is a public folder that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.13 or 5.7.135 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-13-or-5-7-135-in-exchange-online).

why: The recipient address is a mail user that's set up to reject messages sent from outside its organization. Only an email administrator for the recipient's organization can change this configuration.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 5.7.136 in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-5-7-136-in-exchange-online).

sample: `Your message can't be sent because your trial tenant has exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients (tenant external recipient rate limit)`
why: The number of external recipients emailed in a 24-hour period exceeds the external recipient rate limit in Exchange Online. The limit applies per trial tenant.
fix: The external recipient rate limit is tracked over a 24-hour rolling window. When the count for the most recent 24-hour period falls below the limit, users in the trial tenant can resume sending messages to external recipients. The limit helps prevent the distribution of unsolicited bulk messages.

sample: `Your message can't be sent because your tenant exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients (tenant external recipient rate limit)`
why: The number of external recipients emailed in a 24-hour period exceeds the external recipient rate limit in Exchange Online. The limit applies per tenant.
fix: The external recipient rate limit is tracked over a 24-hour rolling window. When the count for the most recent 24-hour period falls below the limit, users in the tenant can resume sending messages to external recipients. The limit helps prevent the distribution of unsolicited bulk messages.

sample: `Your message can't be sent because your tenant has exceeded its daily limit for sending email to external recipients from your tenant's onmicrosoft.com domains`
why: Your organization exceeded the limit of sending emails to 100 external recipients from your organization’s onmicrosoft.com (MOERA) domain within a 24‑hour rolling window. This limit is enforced per tenant.
fix: MOERA (onmicrosoft.com) domains are intended only for testing, and shouldn't be used to send regular email messages. Messages sent from these domains are limited to 100 external recipients for a rolling 24-hour period. Inbound emails aren't affected. External recipients are counted after any recipient list expansion. To avoid this limit, purchase and migrate to a custom domain. Then, make sure that only the custom domain is used to send email messages to external recipients.

sample: `starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail.`
why:
- DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server doesn't respond to the `STARTTLS` command.
- The destination server responds to the `STARTTLS` command, but the TLS handshake fails.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination mail server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine if the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages.

sample: `certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate is expired.`
why: DNSSEC checks passed. However, upon establishing the connection, the destination mail server provides a certificate that's expired.
fix: A valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired must be presented. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, most commonly on an annual basis.

why:
Records are DNSSEC authentic but one or more of the following things occurred:
- The destination mail server's certificate doesn't match what is expected per the authentic TLSA record.
- The authentic TLSA record is misconfigured.
- The destination domain is being attacked.
- The certificate start date is in the future.
- Any other DANE failure.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue exists on the destination mail server. Check the validity of the recipient address and determine if the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages.  For more information about DANE, see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7671.

sample: `dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records`
why: The destination domain indicated it was DNSSEC authentic but Exchange Online wasn't able to verify it as DNSSEC authentic.
fix: For more information about DNSSEC, see [Overview of DNSSEC](/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2012-R2-and-2012/jj200221%28v=ws.11%29).

sample: `certificate-host-mismatch: Remote certificate MUST have a common name or subject alternative name matching the hostname (DANE)`
why: This error occurs if the presented certificate identities (CN and SAN) of a destination SMTP target host don't match any of the domains or MX host.
fix: This message usually indicates an issue on the destination email server. Check the validity of recipient address and determine whether the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages. For more information, see [How SMTP DNS-based Authentication of Named Entities (DANE) works to secure email communications](/en-us/microsoft-365/compliance/how-smtp-dane-works).

sample: `Remote server returned not permitted to relay`
why: This error occurs because of SPF or DKIM authentication failures in forwarded or relayed emails. This problem occurs more frequently in mail flows that include non-Microsoft gateways.
fix: For more information, see [Forwarded or relayed email messages from Microsoft 365 are rejected with error 5.7.367](forwarded-message-rejected-5-7-367-ndr).

why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
fix: For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error code 451 5.7.500-699 (ASxxx) in Exchange Online](fix-error-code-451-4-7-500-699-asxxx-in-exchange-online).  Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset the account credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact Microsoft Support through your regular channel.

why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
fix: Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset its credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact support through your regular channel.

why: The sending account was banned because of detected spam activity.
fix: Verify that account issues are resolved, and reset its credentials. To restore this account's ability to send mail, contact support through your regular channel.

why: The recipient address that you're trying to contact isn't valid.
fix: Verify the recipient's email address, and try again.

why: The recipient that you're trying to contact isn't valid.
fix: If you feel this is an error, contact support.

why: Your server is trying to introduce itself (HELO according to RFC 821) as the server it's trying to connect to, rather than its own fully qualified domain name.
fix: This behavior isn't allowed, and it's characteristic of typical spambot behavior.

why: The recipient's organization blocked the IP from which you're trying to send.
fix: To resolve this issue, contact the recipient.

sample: `Access denied, [$SenderIPAddress] has exceeded permitted limits within $range range`
why: The sender's IPv6 range tried to send too many messages in too short a time period.
fix: Not applicable

sample: `Access denied, sending domain [$SenderDomain] does not pass DMARC verification and has a DMARC policy of reject.`
why: The sender's domain in the **5322.From** address doesn't pass DMARC.
fix: For information about why this error occurred, see Why does DMARC fail?. A user also receives this bounce message because it failed DMARC, and the DMARC policy is set to reject all failures. The user should contact their email administrator for more help.

sample: `Access denied, [contoso.com] does not accept email over IPv6`
why: The sender is trying to transmit a message to the recipient over IPv6, but the recipient doesn't accept email messages over IPv6.
fix: Not applicable

why: The IP that you're trying to send from was banned.
fix: To delist the address, email delist@microsoft.com and provide the full NDR code and IP address.  For more information, see [Use the delist portal to remove yourself from the blocked senders list](/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/use-the-delist-portal-to-remove-yourself-from-the-office-365-blocked-senders-lis).

sample: `Access denied, message must be RFC 5322 section 3.6.2 compliant`
why: Message was sent without a valid "From" email address.
fix: Office 365 only. Each message must contain a valid email address in the "From" header field. Proper formatting of this address includes angle brackets around the email address. For example: <security@contoso.com>. Without an address in this format, Microsoft 365 or Office 365 rejects the message.

sample: `Service unavailable, Client host [$ConnectingIP] blocked by $recipientDomain using Customer Block list (AS16012607)`
why: The recipient domain added your sending IP address to its custom block list.
fix: The domain that received the email message blocked your sender's IP address. If you believe that your IP address was added to the recipient domain's custom block list in error, contact the recipient directly and ask them to remove it.

sample: `Access denied, Your organization does not allow external forwarding. Please contact your administrator for further assistance. AS(7555)`
why: When Exchange Online detects that a message is forwarded automatically, and an outbound spam filter policy blocks the forwarding activity, the message is restricted and this NDR is sent to the sender.
fix: For more information, see [Control automatic external email forwarding](/en-us/defender-office-365/outbound-spam-policies-external-email-forwarding).

why: The IP that you're trying to send from was banned.
fix: Verify that you're following the [best practices for email deliverability](/en-us/dynamics365/marketing/get-ready-email-marketing), and make sure that your IP's reputations aren't degraded because of compromise or malicious traffic. If you believe that you're receiving this message in error, use the self-service portal to request that your IP address be removed from this list.  For more information, see [Use the delist portal to remove yourself from the blocked senders list](/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/use-the-delist-portal-to-remove-yourself-from-the-office-365-blocked-senders-lis).

sample: `Your message can't be delivered because messages to XXX, YYY are blocked by your organization using Tenant Allow Block List.`
why: Someone in your organization sent mail to an email address or domain that's blocked in the [Tenant Allow/Block List](/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/tenant-allow-block-list-about#block-entries-in-the-tenant-allowblock-list). The whole message is blocked for all internal and external recipients of the message, even if only one recipient email address or domain is defined in a block entry.

sample: `5.7.705 Access denied, tenant has exceeded threshold`, `5.7.708 Access denied, traffic not accepted from this IP`
why: Most of the traffic from this tenant is detected as suspicious. Therefore, a ban is put on the sending ability of the tenant.
fix: Make sure that any compromises or open relays were resolved, and then contact support through your regular channel.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error codes 5.7.700 through 5.7.750 in Exchange Online](https://support.microsoft.com/topic/f5675801-1846-4d1c-9599-5b4e26a9175d).

sample: `Service unavailable. Client blocked from sending from unregistered domains`
why: A suspicious number of messages from unprovisioned domains is coming from this tenant.
fix: Add and validate any or all domains that you use to send email from Microsoft 365 or Office 365.  For more information, see [Fix email delivery issues for error codes 5.7.700 through 5.7.750 in Exchange Online](/en-us/exchange/mail-flow-best-practices/non-delivery-reports-in-exchange-online/fix-error-code-5-7-700-through-5-7-750).

why: The EHLO, P1, or P2 sender domain of this message was banned because of detected spam activity.
fix: To restore this domain's ability to send mail, contact Microsoft support.
